newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish 2001 bond auction seen attractive - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Finnish 2001 bond auction seen attractive - analysts.

text.p: Analysts expect the Finnish State Treasury to auction the maximum amount, 1.5 billion markka, of the 2001 bond early on Thursday afternoon.
"...In contrast to several recent auctions we expect the State Treasury Office to succeed in selling the entire amount," Merita research said in a pre-auction comment dated December 5.
The STO has limited the issuance of today's auction to 1.5 billion markka.
Analysts said a recent bull run had dampened buying interest in longer maturities and thus there could be some switching to shorter periods.
"The short end has not come down nearly as much as the longer periods," said Teijo Rantatupa, analyst at OKOBANK, referring to yields on government bonds.
The yield spread between the 2001 bond and the longest benchmark 2006 bond has narrowed to 126 basis points (bps) from 145 bps three weeks ago.
"The 2001 is clearly not as expensive on the yield curve as it used to be," one dealer said.
"...the 2001 is attractive, especially relative to five year Germany where the spread has widened to 30 bps," Merita said.
But some analysts were not as upbeat, saying the approaching year-end could reduce interest in the auction with many investors closing their books for 1996.
"I think we'll see accumulated demand in January with big volumes," Postipankki's Tarja Heinonen said.
"At the start of the year there will be more buying in the short-end as well," she added. @
Analysts said the 2001 bond auction outcome would be close to the current yield level of 5.00 percent give or take a few basis points.
"(It) will be between 4.98 and 5.00 percent," Rantatupa said.
The State Treasury's auction results are due after 1330/1130 GMT and bids should be entered by 1300/1100 GMT through primary dealers.
